# peakhour_rp_ssl_certificate (Resource)

Uploads and tracks the currently configured RP SSL certificate for a domain. Note: the API does not return the uploaded private key (or certificate PEM), so Terraform cannot automatically verify drift of those values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "peakhour_rp_ssl_certificate" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"
  verify = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Domain name.

### Optional

- `certificate_pem` (String) Certificate PEM to upload. Optional; when unset, Terraform will only read certificate info from the API.
- `private_key_pem` (String, Sensitive) Private key PEM to upload. Optional; required if certificate_pem is set. Stored in Terraform state (sensitive).
- `verify` (Boolean) Whether to verify the certificate/private key on upload (default: true).

### Read-Only

- `alt_name` (String) Certificate subjectAltName (computed).
- `cn` (String) Certificate common name (computed).
- `id` (String) RP SSL certificate identifier (domain/rp_ssl_certificate).
- `issuer` (String) Certificate issuer (computed).
- `valid_from` (String) Certificate validity start time (computed).
- `valid_to` (String) Certificate validity end time (computed).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import peakhour_rp_ssl_certificate.example example.com
```
